decisions.reason: Having already carried this fouling detection system through launch and another year of public offering, management is likely to justify the investment and keep it because it fits the firm's move toward smarter monitoring and efficiency and any weak uptake can still be attributed to temporary adoption delays.

This spring-controlled flap weir is close to the core business and still very new, so management would tend to persist with it rather than admit a premature reversal after development and market introduction.

The energy management system sits squarely in the firm's announced strategic direction of digitally networked, efficient, environmentally oriented infrastructure, making management especially prone to continue backing it after a visible launch.

Because the overflow flap gate was introduced as a product line with several models and its own page, the firm has made a relatively strong public and resource commitment and is therefore likely to keep it unless results become clearly untenable.
